vectors.name: a-vanished-subhash-id-is-not-a-dropped-block-stay
vectors.note: SPEC.md §16 mandatory reader rule (v1.6): a tool MUST NOT report a marker carrying the exact `subhash` key as the stay of the block containing it. The key is compared exactly, without segmenting or resolving a child, so a tool that implements neither §5.5 nor §5.6 still applies it. The list and the doomed paragraph both vanish. Only `b2` is a dropped block stay; `c1` never was one, so an implementation whose block id index still admits `subhash` markers reports two DROPPED_IDs here and sends a caller looking for a block that never existed. Since v1.9 `c1`'s loss is still reported, as DROPPED_CHILD_ID: a list item deleted with its stay is treated like a section deleted with its stay, a blocking loss the editor confirms rather than a silent one.

vectors.name: a-child-stay-stripped-from-a-surviving-item-is-dropped
vectors.note: SPEC.md §16 (v1.9): a child stay is a stay, so the before/after diff reports its loss, under DROPPED_CHILD_ID rather than DROPPED_ID so the §16 reader rule still holds (a `subhash` marker is never reported as its container's stay). The test is lexical: the id sat on exactly one marker in the baseline, that marker carried the exact `subhash` key, and no marker carries the id after the edit. No §5.5 or §5.6 segmentation is needed, so every implementation applies it. This is the failure the rule exists for: the item text survives and only its marker went, so nothing but the id set can see it. The container's hash is over marker-stripped content, so it does not drift either.
